title: Rest of the Ellington show: Harry Richman, Mills Brothers, Herb Jeffries
summary: Green recounts the order of acts, with Richman, Mills and Mills, Herb Jeffries singing Prelude to a Kiss, then dancers; Ellington was rarely in America for long.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So, continue with the format of the show.
Well, that's it. He was in the show also -- Harry Richmond, see. He came on after the Mao Brothers, you see. Then after he was on there, then Mills and Mills -- they

came out, (unintelligible). And then some more of the orchestra -- Duke Ellington's orchestra, you see. And he done "Prelude to a Kiss." And I think he was in the works of this song -- it never did become too popular, but it got recognition, you know. It was some kind of ballad -- yes, it did. Herb Jeffries -- I think -- he sang it. He was the vocalist. After that, then, back to the dancers, you know.
